hook: Brook trout crowd into a cold mountain stream in spring. In a hot, dry August the same stream warms by several degrees, and the trout gather in the few shaded pools fed by cold springs. A little warmer still and they stop feeding and growing; warmer again and they die. Every species has a band of conditions it can live in, and that band decides where it can be found.

prereq.q: Which of these is an abiotic factor in a stream?
prereq.why: Abiotic factors are nonliving: temperature, light, water, salinity. Algae, trout and mayflies are biotic.

prereq.q: Which change usually lowers the amount of dissolved oxygen that water can hold?
prereq.why: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen than cold water.

figure.caption: Range of tolerance for water temperature in an invented fish species: an optimal range, zones of physiological stress, and zones of intolerance where none survive.

chain.cause: An abiotic factor, such as temperature, moves out of a species’ optimal range
chain.effect: individuals enter a zone of physiological stress: they grow, feed or reproduce less

chain.cause: Stress lasts or the factor moves further out
chain.effect: fewer individuals survive and reproduce, so the population shrinks

chain.cause: The factor passes the limit of tolerance
chain.effect: individuals die (the zone of intolerance), and the population disappears from that place or moves

ideas: Each species has a range of tolerance for each abiotic factor (temperature, salinity, light, water): the conditions it can survive in.
Inside the range, the optimal range is where individuals grow and reproduce best, and the population is largest.
Toward the edges are zones of physiological stress: individuals survive but feed, grow or reproduce poorly, so the population is small. Beyond the limits lie zones of intolerance, where none survive.
Tolerance applies to individuals and to whole populations. Individuals in a population vary, so some tolerate a little more than others.

misconception.wrong: If a fish survives in water that is too warm, it is doing fine.
misconception.right: Surviving is not thriving. In the zone of physiological stress fish live but eat, grow and reproduce less, so the population shrinks even before any fish die.

summary: Every species has a range of tolerance for each abiotic factor. In the optimal range individuals thrive and populations are largest; in the zones of physiological stress they survive but grow and reproduce poorly; beyond the limits, in the zones of intolerance, they die. Where conditions move out of a species’ range, its population shrinks, moves or disappears.
